requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The active PAM quality configuration sets minlen=12 with all character credits disabled, making 12 an absolute minimum. Direct checks rejected an 11-character password and accepted a compliant 12-character password, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The active configuration sets minclass=3. Direct quality-engine and live PAM password-change tests rejected a long single-class password, while compliant four-class passwords were accepted before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations consistently show Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic. The installed pwquality and cracklib components came from Xenial repositories and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Password length and character-class policy is configured, behaviorally verified, persistent across restart, and implemented with Xenial-compatible packages without changing the OS release or kernel. The mandatory node-restart protocol is coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered policy and system health were all captured and independently corroborated.
limitations: Live PAM testing exercised the character-class rejection and compliant-password acceptance paths, while the exact 11-versus-12 length boundary was tested through the same pwquality engine rather than through a separate live PAM password-change attempt.
Acceptance was demonstrated with four character classes rather than exactly three; the exact three-class threshold is established by the observed minclass=3 configuration and rejection behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installations and policy edits directly implemented or verified the requested policy; temporary probe accounts were removed. The initial unprivileged package-install attempt did not acquire the package lock and shows no mutation. Restart-related temporary state left no observed residue, and final observations show no failed services, unexpected listening sockets, or package damage.
